opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E026 (Alyssa Rose) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the role (Payroll Specialist), which does not apply. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E026 (Alyssa Rose) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes for E026 conflict on employment type: one (HR) says full-time Analyst, max write; the other (Security) says contractor with basic training, for whom write is not permitted (only read, since advanced training is absent). Under the stricter, more restrictive reading required by policy, E026's maximum is read. Granting read is the only level valid under both interpretations, and it is at/below the requested level's intent. Decision: read.
